Kimberly,

Thanks for the materials submitted earlier. Our procurement/legal team finished a first pass and has a short supplemental set of asks focused on IP assignment, third-party model components (open-source/third-party weights), and the liability cap as applied to multi-year committed spend. Please see the attached spreadsheet (Novacore_RFP_Legal_Questions.xlsx) — column B requests short answers we can include in our legal summary.

High-level asks:
- Confirm whether any Redwood-supplied model weights include third-party licenses that would require passthrough obligations.
- For outputs generated using Redwood-hosted models, confirm ownership and license language we can include in our order form.
- Provide a mapping table showing how your proposed liability cap scales with committed spend (year 1, year 2, 3-year total).

Can you share updated responses by COB Thursday (2026-11-19)? We also want a redlined order form (if you have a standard) so our legal ops can begin internal approvals.

Attaching spreadsheet.

Elena / Samir / Novacore team —

Thanks for the clear list. We've completed a written supplement and attached the completed workbook (Redwood_Filled_RFP_Novacore.xlsx) plus our standard order form (Redwood_Proposed_Order_Form_v1.pdf). Key notes up front:

- Third-party model components: our curated model catalog includes both open-source and Redwood-trained variants. Where open-source weights are used, we identify the license in the model catalog and provide customers with the applicable license text; customers are responsible for complying with any copyleft obligations in their use of those models. For Redwood-verified variants (our tuned checkpoints), Redwood grants customers a non-exclusive, worldwide license to use the model for inference via the Redwood service. We do not claim ownership of customer data or customer outputs.

- Outputs and ownership: Customer retains ownership of data they submit and the outputs generated from that data. Redwood provides a limited license to the customer for the service (inference and API) and provides standard usage rights in the order form. See sheet 'Ownership' in the attached workbook for suggested language.

- Liability cap mapping: we included a matrix showing proposed caps by committed annual spend. In short, standard cap = the greater of (3x fees paid in the trailing 12 months) or $2.5M for self-serve / hosted customers; for reserved (Dedicated) commitments we can negotiate higher caps tied to committed ARR (see sheet 'Liability_Matrix'). For enterprise customers with an approved SOW we can discuss $5M caps with indemnity carveouts.

- Indemnity: Redwood's indemnity covers third-party IP infringement claims arising from the service as provided; we exclude claims arising from (i) customer data that introduces third-party IP, (ii) customer modifications to redwood software, and (iii) use of third-party models where obligations pass-through to the customer.

We flagged the precise suggested order-form language in the PDF (comments enabled). Please review — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the workbook.

Kimberly Park

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups after our internal review: 

1) Can you clarify the practical effect of "non-exclusive license to use the model for inference via the Redwood service" — specifically, do we get any portability of tuned checkpoints or weights if we move to a private deployment? Novacore needs to understand migration constraints.

2) Your liability cap language references 3x fees or $2.5M; Novacore legal is asking for a simpler table: for committed spends of <$250k/year, cap $1M; $250k-$2M: cap $3M; >$2M/year: cap $5M. Can Redwood confirm willingness to adopt a range like this for an enterprise order?

3) On indemnity for third-party models, please specify which license families (e.g., GPL-style copyleft, AGPL, Apache 2.0, MIT/BSD) Redwood will accept on behalf of the customer vs pass-through.

We'd like to firm answers by EOD Friday (2026-11-20).

—Samir
Director, Cloud Platform — Novacore

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: legal questionnaire - supplemental items

Samir / Elena —

Thanks — below are the clarifications you requested. I've quoted the relevant workbook cells where helpful.

1) Portability / private deployment: For Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem), the customer's access to tuned checkpoints depends on the deployment model: 
- For fully managed Private where Redwood hosts the model within the customer's VPC, we can provide a copy of tuned artifacts under a restricted use license (customer may use for inference within their environment but cannot re-distribute).
- For air-gapped on-prem deployments, we offer an export process subject to export controls and export-approval timing; this is captured as a scope item in the order form. We cannot provide portability for models that include third-party-prohibited redistribution terms. (Workbook ref: 'Model_Portability' row).

2) Liability caps by tier: Redwood is open to negotiating a stepped cap similar to the bands you proposed for enterprise commitments. As initial offer: <$250k/yr = $1M cap; $250k–$2M/yr = $3M cap; >$2M/yr = $5M cap, subject to approval for Dedicated commitments and formal SOW. We will require a minimum committed ARR to qualify for the higher caps. Please see the annotated 'Liability_Matrix' sheet (cells C2:C6) for the proposed mapping.

3) Third-party license families: Redwood will accept responsibility (i.e., indemnify) for claims arising from our distribution of third-party components only where the license is permissive (MIT, BSD, Apache 2.0) and we supply the weight as part of Redwood-hosted service. We do not assume indemnity for copyleft licenses that impose redistribution obligations (GPL/AGPL) — in such cases the obligation remains with the user. For practical purposes, we flag any model in the catalog that includes a copyleft requirement. (Workbook ref: 'Licenses' tab).

Next steps: Marissa / Aditya / Jonas — can you review the order-form comments and confirm whether Pricing / Sales are comfortable with the proposed cap bands and the export process language? If yes, we'll prepare a redline for Novacore to review.

Kimberly
